name: Standing hamstring curl
summary: Standing tall, bend one knee to bring the heel toward the buttock, thigh staying still.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, hands on a wall or chair in front, working leg nearest the phone. Keeping the thigh pointing straight down, bend the knee to lift the heel behind you, then lower with control.
brief: Hands on a wall or chair in front, working leg. Keeping the thigh pointing straight down, bend the knee to lift the heel behind you, then lower with control.
why: From the side the knee angle gives the curl, and the thigh swinging forward — the way people cheat — shows as the hip–knee line leaving vertical.
progression: Ankle weight or band around the ankles.
regression: Smaller bend, or lying on your front.
contraindications: Cramp or sharp pain at the back of the thigh.

faults.label: Thigh swinging forward
faults.tip: The hip should not move — only the knee bends. Squeeze the buttock to keep the thigh pointing down.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace the stomach lightly so the back does not sway as the heel rises.

faults.label: Thigh drifting forward
faults.tip: If the thigh comes forward the hip is helping. Keep both knees level with each other.

faults.label: Short of a right angle
faults.tip: Bend until the knee is at least ninety; short curls miss the range that matters.

guide.surface: Firm floor; something solid to hold in front.
guide.stop: Hamstring cramp or a sharp pull.
guide.cannotSee: The back arching, and the foot turning in or out.

points.t: Thigh vertical and still; only the knee bends.
Heel travels toward the buttock, not out to the side.
Tall, light hands on the support.
